content.title: How To Watch Villanova Wildcats Men's Basketball
content.text: ✦ Edited and fact-checked by Mike Strayer, our Managing Editor with over 11 years of covering sports and TV. A look at the 2025–2026 Wildcats The Wildcat Way has a new architect, and the results are finally matching the pedigree. After a frustrating three-year absence from the Big Dance, Villanova is back where it belongs. Kevin Willard has injected a fresh energy into the program, blending a Top-15 recruiting class with strategic portal additions to finish near the top of a punishing Big East. The three-year drought is over, and the hunger in Philadelphia is palpable. I’ve been particularly impressed by how quickly freshman Acaden Lewis and transfer Tyler Perkins have gelled in the backcourt. This team is fun again, playing at a pace and with aggression that were missing during the transition years. While some fans are still debating if this is a one-off portal success or a true return to the Jay Wright standard, there is no denying that ‘Nova is a dangerous #8 seed that nobody wants to see in their bracket. With the Wildcats heading across the country to San Diego for their opening game, you’ll need a solid plan to follow the action from home. This guide will show you how to watch Villanova basketball to witness the first chapter of the Willard era in the NCAA Tournament. 2025–2026 Villanova Wildcats basketball TV schedule Villanova’s tournament journey begins on Friday, March 20, against Utah State. This West Region matchup features a late-afternoon tip-off, broadcast nationally on TNT. If the Wildcats can secure a win in San Diego, they’ll likely face a collision course with a top-seeded powerhouse in the Round of 32. viewing experience, Hulu + Live TV is my top pick. It includes TNT for the opening round, plus TBS and truTV for the rest of the tournament’s cable games. Most importantly, it gives you CBS for the high-stakes weekend matchups that determine who goes to the Final Four. It is the most comprehensive package for a fan who wants to see every minute of the Big East’s finest. If you are looking to save a bit of cash, you can stream ‘Nova’s first-round game on TNT via the HBO Max app. You will need the B/R Sports Add-on to access the live feed, but it’s a high-quality stream that works on almost any device. This is a great quick fix for the early rounds, though you’ll eventually need a way to get CBS if the Wildcats make a deep run into the second weekend. Whatever you do, stay away from Fubo for March Madness. Because Fubo doesn’t carry TNT, TBS, or truTV, you would miss the Utah State game entirely. Stick with Hulu + Live TV or YouTube TV to ensure you have the right channels for the Wildcats’ return to glory. How to watch Villanova basketball FAQ How can I watch Villanova for free? You can watch Villanova for free by using a digital antenna for any games broadcast on CBS. For cable games on TNT or TBS, you might consider signing up for a free trial of a streaming service like YouTube TV or DIRECTV during the tournament. How can I stream Villanova without cable? I recommend streaming Villanova via Hulu + Live TV, which carries TNT, TBS, truTV, and CBS. Another excellent option for the cable-hosted games is the HBO Max app, provided you have the B/R Sports Add-on active. Can I watch Villanova on TNT? Yes, you can watch Villanova on TNT for their first-round game against Utah State. TNT is available on almost all major cable providers and live TV streaming services like Hulu + Live TV and Sling TV. How can I watch Villanova in March Madness? Villanova's March Madness games are split between CBS, TBS, TNT, and truTV. You can also track the games live on the March Madness Live website or app by logging in with your streaming or cable credentials. Why you should trust us Our CableTV.com editorial team cross-referenced the official Villanova Wildcats schedule with the channel lineups of every major TV provider. Using those details, we selected our viewing recommendations based on channel availability, pricing, and ease of use. This guide is updated regularly throughout the season to ensure our information is accurate. To learn more about our methods, check out our How We Rank page.
